findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — P1, confidence 100: After deleting the date-range filtering and start/end/statsPeriod serializer fields, `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` proceeds directly to pagination on the organization/actor/event queryset, so existing requests specifying start/end or statsPeriod silently receive audit entries outside their requested time window even when optimized pagination is disabled.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — P1, confidence 100: `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` receives a datetime from the audit endpoint’s `order_by="-datetime"`, so every nonempty optimized first page raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` while building its cursors; unlike DateTimePaginator this class also leaves numeric cursor values unconverted for timestamp comparisons.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — P2, confidence 100: `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` passes an explicitly negative `start_offset` to a Django QuerySet when advanced pagination receives a cursor such as `0:-1:0`, which Django rejects because negative indexing is unsupported, so the advertised negative-offset navigation fails before fetching any rows.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — P1, confidence 100: An authorized optimized audit-log request with at least one row fails during cursor construction because `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` receives the datetime selected by `order_by="-datetime"` and raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`, while `return cursor.value` also omits the timestamp-to-datetime conversion required when resuming a DateTimePaginator cursor.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — P2, confidence 100: The advertised advanced negative-offset path passes `start_offset = cursor.offset` to `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`, so an optimized request with `cursor=0:-1:0` raises Django's negative-indexing error before returning any page instead of supporting the requested navigation or rejecting the cursor as a client error.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — P1, confidence 100: Replacing the existing `queryset = queryset.filter(datetime__range=(start, end))` date-filtering block with `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` expands a pagination-performance change into removal of the endpoint’s time-range contract, so audit-log consumers supplying `start`/`end` or `statsPeriod` receive records outside their requested window even without opting into optimized pagination.

goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — P1, confidence 100: An authorized optimized audit-log request with at least one row fails during cursor construction because `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` receives the datetime selected by `order_by="-datetime"` and raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`, while `return cursor.value` also omits the timestamp-to-datetime conversion required when resuming a DateTimePaginator cursor.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() at line 840 does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` then `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))`. When used with `order_by="-datetime"`, self.key would be 'datetime', so value would be a datetime object. Calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime raises TypeError. The DateTimePaginator handles this by converting datetime to timestamp, but OptimizedCursorPaginator lacks this conversion. Similarly, value_from_cursor just returns cursor.value without datetime conversion. This is a real bug that would cause crashes when the paginator is used with datetime fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — P2, confidence 100: The advertised advanced negative-offset path passes `start_offset = cursor.offset` to `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`, so an optimized request with `cursor=0:-1:0` raises Django's negative-indexing error before returning any page instead of supporting the requested navigation or rejecting the cursor as a client error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result() at lines 879-884, when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0, the code sets start_offset = cursor.offset (a negative value) and then does queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing in slicing - this will raise an AssertionError or similar error. The finding correctly identifies that this code path will fail at runtime rather than either working as intended or returning a proper client error.
